scenarios.description: A transfer between two scopes of an account moves the balance from one scope to the other.
A balance record's balance is in its account's currency.
A scope whose balance is below the minimum is not found.
A scope whose balance is above the minimum is found.
A scope whose balance equals the minimum is found.
Each account's balance record holds the same balance as the account.
A transfer between two accounts of one scope moves the balance between them.
Each scope of an account has a balance and a balance record of its own.
With a fixer, a check that finds a wrong balance record sets it to the recalculated balance.
With a fixer, a check that finds a wrong line balance recalculates the account's running balances and its balance record.
With a fixer, a wrong line balance in another currency is recalculated in that currency.
A blank scope or scope identity counts as none: it finds the unscoped account, and a scoped account asked for with a blank scope raises UnknownAccount.

Account.currency gives the currency of the account defined with an identifier, scoped or not: USD, the default, for one defined without a currency, BHD for one defined with it; an identifier no account has gives nil.
An account defined without a currency has Money.default_currency, USD.
Defining the same identifier twice raises DuplicateAccount.
Two instances of an account with the same scope are equal and hash alike; with different scopes they are neither.
An account defined with currency AUD has AUD.
A scoped account is found with a scope, whose id is its scope identity as a string, or with a scope identity given as is.
An unscoped account is found by its identifier alone; it has no scope identity.
With account_identifier_max_length 31, an identifier of 31 characters is accepted.
With account_identifier_max_length 31, an identifier of 32 characters raises AccountIdentifierTooLongError.
With scope_identifier_max_length 23, a scope identity of 23 characters is accepted.
A scope_identifier that raises makes DoubleEntry.account raise the same error.
With scope_identifier_max_length 23, a scope identity of 24 characters raises ScopeIdentifierTooLongError.
Asking for a scoped account without a scope raises UnknownAccount.
Account instances sort by scope identity, then identifier, both as strings; an unscoped account sorts as an empty scope identity.
to_s writes the identifier, the scope as given and the currency.
An identifier that was not defined raises UnknownAccount.
Asking for an unscoped account with a scope raises UnknownAccount.
A transfer takes its amount from the origin's balance and adds it to the destination's.
A balance at a time is the running balance of the last line created at or before it.
With at beside from and to, the balance is the running balance at that time: the range is ignored and nothing is summed.
A balance at a time with microseconds counts a line created at or before it, to the microsecond (U-15).
With at beside a code or codes, the balance is the sum of the amounts of the lines created at or before at with any of those codes, not a running balance.
A balance between two times is the sum of the amounts of the lines created between them, both ends included.
A balance between now and a time in the future sums the lines written in the future.
A balance between times with microseconds sums the lines created between them, both ends included, to the microsecond (U-15).
DoubleEntry.balance with an identifier and a scope gives the balance of that account instance.
A balance by code is the sum of the amounts of the account's lines with that code.
A balance by codes sums the lines with any of them; a code given beside codes is one more of them.
With from but no to, or to but no from, there is no range: the balance is the running balance of the account's last line, nothing summed.
Without options a balance is the running balance of the account's last line, even one written in the future, in the account's currency.
Each line of an account holds the account's running balance after it.
DoubleEntry.balance with a scope its account's scope_identifier rejects raises the scope_identifier's error.
DoubleEntry.balance of a scoped account without a scope raises UnknownAccount.
Unconfigured, the three max lengths are nil, json_metadata is false and running_inside_transactional_fixtures is false.
A max length that has been set is read back as set: code 10, scope identifier 11, account identifier 9.
A balance record that differs from the running balance is an error on the account; without a fixer the record stays wrong.
A check of consistent lines persists a LineCheck without errors, up to the last line, with an empty log.
last_line_id_checked is the last_line_id of the newest check by created_at, not the last one created.
A line whose balance is not the previous balance plus its amount is an error on the line and on its account; without a fixer the balance stays wrong.
A check with no lines since the last check returns nothing and persists no LineCheck.
A check of consistent lines in another currency than the default finds no errors.
A wrong line balance in another currency is an error on the line and on its account, logged in that currency; without a fixer the balance stays wrong.
A line's account and partner account are account instances, with the scope identities the line was saved with.
A line has its amount as Money and its code as given; a line saved without a detail keeps its code after a reload.
Line.credits lists the lines with a positive amount and Line.debits those with a negative one, the other way round from the transfer's names (U-07).
A line takes its currency from its account.
The credit is a decrease and the debit an increase.
Saving a positive balance on a negative-only account raises AccountWouldBeSentPositiveError.
A line without a code is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint of the code column.
The credit and the debit are each other's partner, and the pair puts the credit first.
Saving a negative balance on a positive-only account raises AccountWouldBeSentNegative.
Assigning an unscoped account sets the account column and leaves the scope null, for the partner account too.
A balance record created by a lock takes its balance from the last line of the account.
Locking an account without a balance record creates one, with a zero balance.
A mysql deadlock inside with_restart_on_deadlock publishes deadlock_restart and restarts the transaction, so the lock goes through.
A postgres deadlock inside with_restart_on_deadlock publishes deadlock_restart and restarts the transaction, so the lock goes through.
A sqlite deadlock inside with_restart_on_deadlock publishes deadlock_restart and restarts the transaction, so the lock goes through.
create_ignoring_duplicates! retries the create on a mysql deadlock, publishing deadlock_retry on each retry.
create_ignoring_duplicates! retries the create on a postgres deadlock, publishing deadlock_retry on each retry.
create_ignoring_duplicates! retries the create on a sqlite deadlock, publishing deadlock_retry on each retry.
create_ignoring_duplicates! ignores the RecordNotUnique of a duplicate username and publishes duplicate_ignore.
create_ignoring_duplicates! re-raises a StatementInvalid that is neither a duplicate nor a deadlock, and publishes nothing.
restartable_transaction runs its block again while it raises RestartTransaction.
Locking inside a regular transaction raises LockMustBeOutermostTransaction.
A scoped and an unscoped account are locked together; both get a balance record.
With json_metadata, a key with an array of values stores the array in both lines' metadata column and creates no line_metadata rows.
With json_metadata, a transfer without metadata creates no line_metadata rows and leaves the lines' metadata column empty.
With json_metadata, a transfer with two key/value pairs stores them in both lines' metadata column and creates no line_metadata rows.
Without json_metadata, a key with an array of values creates one line_metadata row per value and line, and leaves the lines' metadata column empty.
On the generator's tables without json_metadata, the metadata goes to line_metadata, and a line has no metadata reader: Line#metadata raises NoMethodError.
Without json_metadata, a transfer without metadata creates no line_metadata rows and leaves the lines' metadata column empty.
Without json_metadata, a transfer with two key/value pairs creates one line_metadata row per pair and line, and leaves the lines' metadata column empty.
A StatementInvalid matching /lock wait timeout/ while locking raises LockWaitTimeout.
A nested lock of accounts the outer lock holds goes through.
A nested lock of an account the outer lock does not hold raises LockNotHeld.
Any other StatementInvalid while locking is re-raised as it is.
A transfer rolled back by ActiveRecord::Rollback inside a lock leaves both balances at zero.
An exception after a transfer inside a lock propagates, and the transfer is rolled back.
With running_inside_transactional_fixtures, a lock inside a regular transaction goes through.
A transfer inside a lock of both its accounts goes through.
A transfer inside a lock that does not hold its destination raises LockNotHeld.
With json_metadata the migration adds a json metadata column to the lines and creates no line_metadata table.
Without json_metadata the migration creates the line_metadata table and the lines have no metadata column.
With code_max_length 47, a code of 47 characters is accepted.
With code_max_length 47, a code of 48 characters raises TransferCodeTooLongError.
Defining the same from, to and code twice raises DuplicateTransfer.
Two rules between the same accounts with different codes are both found, by find and by find!.
find! raises TransferNotAllowed for a rule that was not defined (the reverse direction).
find returns nothing for a rule that was not defined (the reverse direction).
An allowed transfer writes a credit and a debit line and the two account balances.
A transfer from an account defaulting to USD to one given currency 'USD' (U-05).
A transfer from an account given currency 'USD' to one defaulting to USD (U-05).
A transfer from an account to itself, with the same scope, raises TransferNotAllowed even when a rule allows it.
A transfer inside a regular transaction raises LockMustBeOutermostTransaction and writes nothing.
An allowed transfer between accounts of different currencies raises MismatchedCurrencies.
A negative amount raises TransferIsNegative before the rule is looked up.
A transfer creates two lines and returns the credit, the negative amount, then the debit, the positive amount.
A transfer between two scopes of the same account is allowed.
A transfer with a detail writes its type and id on both lines.
A transfer without a code between accounts no rule joins raises TransferNotAllowed.
A transfer with a code no rule has raises TransferNotAllowed.
A transfer against the direction of its rule raises TransferNotAllowed and writes nothing.
A transfer of zero, an amount Transfer.transfer checks only for being negative.
